source_table: section 'Lessons learned from ASO toxicity studies', valeriasen paragraph
notes: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. Consortium-level restatement of the valeriasen experience by the N=1 Collaborative: 'Initially valeriasen was effective at reducing seizure activity in Valeria and a second patient whose treatment commenced after Valeria. Unexpectedly, the ASO resulted in the development of hydrocephalus in both patients. This adverse effect had not been observed in safety studies conducted in healthy rats, but was hypothesized to be specifically due to the pathological state of the human brain.' THIS IS THE KEY TRANSLATIONAL POINT FOR THIS DATASET - a CNS toxicity that healthy-rodent toxicology did not predict, which is precisely the predictive gap the OligoTox challenge is aimed at. The review adds that hydrocephalus and inflammation have been reported with other ASOs and calls for safety-data sharing. This row intentionally DUPLICATES the two primary Nature Medicine patient rows in order to preserve the consortium framing; de-duplicate against the primary source at assembly if only one representation is wanted.

source_table: 'Safety and adverse events' section, patient 2 narrative; Extended Data Fig. 6c
notes: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. PATIENT 2, also a girl aged 3 with KCNT1 p.R474H, enrolled 9 months after patient 1 and about 2 months before hydrocephalus was detected in patient 1. Escalating intrathecal doses of 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg. Brain MRI on day 55 was UNREMARKABLE with normal ventricular size and a normal lumbar opening pressure of 16 cm H2O; repeat MRIs on days 62 and 64 showed MILD INCREASES IN VENTRICULAR SIZE with no evidence of obstruction. Given the finding in patient 1 she was transferred to intensive care for neurologic monitoring, an extraventricular drain was placed (opening pressure >20 cm H2O), drainage was persistent, and a VENTRICULOPERITONEAL SHUNT WAS PLACED ON DAY 65. Ventricular dilatation gradually normalised on serial MR ventriculograms and she was discharged home in stable condition on day 87. GRADE 3 (hydrocephalus requiring intervention) despite complete radiological reversal - the grade reflects the intervention, and reversibility=reversible records the outcome.

notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; n=4 mice/group. Group means not reported numerically and the multi-group bar chart was not digitised. Late-ONSET CNS toxicity: signs appeared at least 3 days after a single central injection, persisted for 6 days or more and worsened over time. The authors emphasise this is distinct from acute toxicity - no acute neurotoxicity was seen with ASO1, ASO3 or ASO4, and the acute toxicity of ASO2 resolved completely within 1 day. Tolerability scoring system in Supplementary Table S2 covers consciousness, motor function (ataxia, strength) and appearance (posture, breathing, home-cage activity). No recovery/reversal phase was run: animals were killed at a scheduled time point or when they reached a humane endpoint, and signs were progressive up to that point, so reversibility is recorded as irreversible on the evidence available rather than demonstrated permanence.
